housing.summary: Melbourne's inner-city 1-bedroom apartment typically rents for approximately AUD 500–600 per week. Victoria's Residential Tenancies Act sets the bond (deposit) at a maximum of 1 month's rent (approximately 4 weeks). Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

banking.summary: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival and accepts new migrants within 12 months of arrival with in-branch ID verification. ANZ offers the ANZ Access Advantage account for new residents with a $5 monthly fee waivable on $2,000+ monthly deposits.
required_docs: Valid passport (original required for in-branch ID verification within 20 days)

schools.summary: Melbourne has numerous international schools offering IB, British, and American curricula. The national directory myschool.edu.au lists all schools. VIC state schools fall under the Department of Education. Notable international-curriculum schools include Haileybury, Carey Baptist Grammar, and the French School (ACFE-affiliated).

legal_admin.summary: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link ATO, Medicare, and Centrelink services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with myGov; notify Home Affairs of address changes

tax_finance.summary: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Apply online for free at ato.gov.au. The TFN is required by employers for payroll tax withholding.

transport.summary: Melbourne's public transport is operated by Public Transport Victoria (PTV) using the myki card system. The network covers metropolitan trains, trams, and buses. A 28-day (monthly) myki Pass for Zone 1+2 (full metro network) costs approximately AUD 181.60. Overseas licence holders visiting Victoria may drive on their foreign licence; those taking up residence must convert to a Victorian licence via VicRoads. Medicare registration for eligible visa holders is via Services Australia.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Overseas licence holders may drive in Victoria on their foreign licence while visiting; upon taking up residency must convert to Victorian licence via VicRoads (vicroads.vic.gov.au). No automatic expiry period but conversion required to become a resident.
transport.healthcare_registration: Eligible visa holders enrol in Medicare at Services Australia offices or online via servicesaustralia.gov.au/medicare.
